## Introduction to Copyright

Copyright represents a collection of exclusive rights held by creators over their original works,
including authority over how their creations are utilised and distributed.
The general principles related to copyright are specified in the Berne Convention, an international treaty 
which has been ratified by the vast majority of countries, and whose main purpose is to provide 
uniformity of copyright and similar rights.

By default, copyright functions under an "all rights reserved" model, restricting others from accessing,
copying, modifying, or sharing work without explicit authorisation. Licences serve as the mechanism to
grant these permissions.

## Copyright at CERTH

At CERTH, employed personnel (including permanent researchers, engineers, and affiliated staff)
typically have the works produced within the scope of their professional activities held by their
respective CERTH Institute as the copyright owner, in accordance with Greek employment and
intellectual property law.

Before publishing any work that incorporates third-party contributions, securing signed agreements or
valid licences from the relevant copyright holders is essential. This applies equally to code,
documentation, datasets, and design files.
